# 3DGS-DR
## Overview
3DGS-DR is a method that incorporates classical reflection and shading concepts into the 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) framework [S1, unofficial]. It addresses the limitation of standard 3DGS, which uses an [emission-absorption model](#927-emission-absorption-model.md) that bakes lighting conditions into [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients, thereby limiting performance on highly reflective surfaces and preventing relighting [S1, unofficial].

## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Inputs:** Multi-view images of a scene.
*   **Outputs:** A set of 3D Gaussians augmented with shading parameters [S1, unofficial]. Exact output layouts are not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

**Data Structures:**
Each Gaussian stores standard 3DGS attributes (position, covariance, opacity) plus parameters for classical reflection and shading [S1, unofficial]. Exact field layouts, sizes, and bit-packing are not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

**Numbered Steps:**
The [training and optimization](#6838-coarse-to-fine-sparse-volume-training.md) steps are not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

**Formulas:**
Pixel color is computed by volume rendering the Gaussians along the ray, where the primitive color term is derived from a classical [shading model](#837-shading-models.md) [S1, unofficial]. The exact BRDF formula and shading computation steps are not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

**Parameters:**
*   BRDF model type: Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].
*   Learning rate: Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
*   **Aliasing:** Standard 3DGS uses a dilation filter which fails to suppress high-frequency artifacts when varying focal length or camera distance [S1, unofficial]. The specific impact or mitigation for 3DGS-DR is not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### iVR-GS Training Setup
A [training configuration](#2332-training-configuration.md) for iVR-GS that uses a [Blinn-Phong shading model](#2239-blinn-phong-shading-model.md) to decompose each Gaussian's color into intrinsic color and lighting components, enabling post-training appearance and illumination editing [S2, unofficial]. It composes multiple base models, each trained under one basic transformation function (TF) [S2, unofficial]. For lighting-free evaluation, training images are generated from DVR renders with lighting disabled to ensure identical rendering settings [S2, unofficial]. Minor brightness variations may persist in rendered outputs despite disabling lighting, due to the inherent view-dependent nature of the [iVR-GS training](#7578-ivr-gs-training.md) formulation [S2, unofficial].

## Operating characteristics
*   **Time Complexity:** Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].
*   **Strengths:** Enables classical reflection and shading, addressing the emission-absorption model's limitation on highly reflective surfaces and enabling relighting [S1, unofficial].
*   **Limitations:** Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].
*   **When to use:** Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].
*   **When not to use:** Not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

## Background
3DGS-DR was introduced to address the limitations of the emission-absorption model in standard 3DGS, which bakes lighting into spherical harmonics and prevents relighting [S1, unofficial]. It is part of a family of methods including GaussianShader and [IRGS](#6003-inverse-rendering-with-inter-reflections-irgs.md) that incorporate classical reflection and shading concepts into the 3DGS framework [S1, unofficial]. The method builds on the 3D Gaussian Splatting foundation [Parent](1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-brdf-embedding.md) [S1, unofficial].
